B.finding: Official collapses visited indices into one pass-token variable X, reduces values to parity, handles N<=3 separately, and states that for N>=4 the parity of the number of odd A_i determines the winner. This matches the frozen M0 classification.

C.finding: Official gives an independent <=2N-1 reconstruction by finding an endpoint with anchor queries, sorting sums from that endpoint, recovering adjacent A differences, and resolving reversal by P1<P2. This corroborates the identifiability and query-budget boundary; frozen M0 uses a different 2N-3 two-anchor derivation.

E.finding: Official derives the same double hockey-stick path-sum identities and subtracts forbidden-region crossing paths via O((R-L)+(U-D)) boundary terms after O(W+H) factorial precomputation. Frozen M0 uses an equivalent unique-first-forbidden-vertex decomposition.
